# Hierarchical PLS_DA Evaluation

```{r}
## Import all results
initial_data <- list(
    "binary_1000" = read.csv("results/hierarchical/2_plsda_1000_results.csv"),
    "binary_1250" = read.csv("results/hierarchical/2_plsda_1250_results.csv"),
    "weighted_1000" = read.csv("results/hierarchical/weighted_triangle_plsda_1000_results.csv"),
    "weighted_1250" = read.csv("results/hierarchical/weighted_triangle_plsda_1250_results.csv")
)

# remove all column except 1 - 5 and 15
data <- lapply(initial_data, function(df) df[, c(1:5, 15)])

# remove Total_DON data on 1000 dataframes
data$binary_1000 <- data$binary_1000[data$binary_1000$Target_toxin != "Total_DON", ]
data$weighted_1000 <- data$weighted_1000[data$weighted_1000$Target_toxin != "Total_DON", ]

# add details about the sample_weight
data$binary_1000$Sample_weight <- "None"
data$binary_1250$Sample_weight <- "None"
data$weighted_1000$Sample_weight <- "Weighted"
data$weighted_1250$Sample_weight <- "Weighted"

# combine all dataframes into one
combined_data <- do.call(rbind, data)

#remove the second derivative data
combined_data <- combined_data[combined_data$Preprocessing != "2nd_Der", ]
str(combined_data)

# except MCC transform all to factor
combined_data[c(1:5, 7)] <- lapply(combined_data[c(1:5, 7)], as.factor)
str(combined_data)

# Apply Fisher transformation to MCC
combined_data$MCC_z <- atanh(combined_data$MCC)

#rename the columns
library(dplyr)
lme_data <- combined_data %>%
 rename(
   Material = Sample_source,
   Toxin = Target_toxin,
   Weighting = Sample_weight
 )
```

## Analysis using Linear mixed-effects
This experiment is performed using Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with 6 factors: Sample_weight, Target_toxin, Preprocessing, Variable_Selection and Sample_weight. The response variable is MCC_z.

```{r}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
# Fit the linear mixed-effects model until three-way interaction
model <- lmer(MCC_z ~ (Material + Toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Weighting)^3 + (1|Split), data = lme_data)
anova(model)

# determine the ICC (intraclass correlation) of the model
library(performance)
icc(model)
r2(model)


summary(model)
print(model, correlation = TRUE)
library(sjPlot)
tab_model(model)

#select the best pipelines
best_pipelines <- emmeans(model, pairwise ~ Material * Toxin * Preprocessing * Variable_Selection * Weighting)
best_pipelines_df <- as.data.frame(best_pipelines$emmeans)
best_pipelines_df <- best_pipelines_df[order(-best_pipelines_df$emmean), ]
best_pipelines_df <- best_pipelines_df[1:10, ]
#conclusion: the best pipeline is the one with the highest emmean value
head(best_pipelines_df)
```

## Plot

## Linear mixed-effects, but using balanced_accuracy instead of MCC as response variable

```{r}
# remove all column except 1 - 5 and balanced_accuracy
data2 <- lapply(initial_data, function(df){
    df$balanced_accuracy <- (df$Sensitivity + df$Specitifity) / 2
    df[, c(names(df)[1:5], "balanced_accuracy"), drop = FALSE]
})

# add details about the sample_weight
data2$binary_1000$Sample_weight <- "None"
data2$binary_1250$Sample_weight <- "None"
data2$weighted_1000$Sample_weight <- "Weighted"
data2$weighted_1250$Sample_weight <- "Weighted"

# combine all dataframes into one
combined_data2 <- do.call(rbind, data2)

#remove the second derivative data
combined_data2 <- combined_data2[combined_data2$Preprocessing != "2nd_Der", ]
str(combined_data2)

# except MCC transform all to factor
combined_data2[c(1:5, 7)] <- lapply(combined_data2[c(1:5, 7)], as.factor)
str(combined_data2)

# Fit the linear mixed-effects model
model2 <- lmer(balanced_accuracy ~ (Sample_source + Target_toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + Sample_weight)^2 + (1|Split), data = combined_data2)
anova(model2)

#select the best pipelines
best_pipelines2 <- emmeans(model2, pairwise ~ Sample_source * Target_toxin * Preprocessing * Variable_Selection * Sample_weight)
best_pipelines2_df <- as.data.frame(best_pipelines2$emmeans)
best_pipelines2_df <- best_pipelines2_df[order(-best_pipelines2_df$emmean), ]
best_pipelines2_df <- best_pipelines2_df[1:10, ]
```


### Physical Effect of Sample Source
```{r}
library(ggpubr)

# Find the maximum MCC to know where to draw the bracket
max_y <- max(combined_data$MCC, na.rm = TRUE)

# 1. Build the clean, publication-ready violin + boxplot in one command
material_plot <- ggviolin(
                    combined_data, 
                    x = "Sample_source", 
                    y = "MCC", 
                    fill = "Sample_source",
                    palette = c("#fde725", "#440154"),
                    add = "boxplot",
                    add.params = list(fill = "white", width = 0.15), 
                    trim = FALSE,
                    legend = "none",
                    title = "Material Effect on Model Performance",
                    subtitle = "Distribution of 960 algorithmic runs across 10 test splits",
                    xlab = "Type of Wheat Material",
                    ylab = "Matthew Correlation Coefficient"
                    ) +
                stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 4, fill = "black") +
  
                # The significance comes from ANOVA type III with Satterthwaite's method
                geom_bracket(
                    xmin = "ground", 
                    xmax = "intact",
                    y.position = max_y + 0.2,
                    label = "***",
                    tip.length = 0.03,
                    label.size = 8,
                    vjust = 0.5
                ) +
                theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/material_plot.svg", plot = material_plot, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", dpi =600)
```

```{r}
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Extract the means of preprocessing, weighting and toxin interaction
emm_toxin <- emmeans(model, ~ Preprocessing * Weighting * Toxin)
toxin_df <- as.data.frame(emm_toxin)

# 2. Build the Faceted Plot
prep_toxin_weight_plot <-ggplot(toxin_df, aes(x = Preprocessing, y = emmean, 
                     color = Weighting, group = Weighting)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE), 
                width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.4) +
  
  # THIS IS THE MAGIC LINE: It splits the plot into two clean panels
  facet_wrap(~ Toxin) + 
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Weighted" = "#e74c3c", "None" = "#34495e")) +
  labs(
    title = "Model Performance Across Toxin Targets",
    subtitle = "Interaction of Preprocessing and Sample Weighting",
    x = "Spectral Preprocessing Method",
    y = "emmean of MCC",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f8f9fa"), # Colors the facet headers
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
  )
prep_toxin_weight_plot
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/prep_toxin_weight_plot.svg", plot = prep_toxin_weight_plot, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in", dpi =600)
```

## Cross-Label between DON and Total DON
```{r}
#import the dataset
library(readxl)
label <- read_excel("./nirs/nirs_intact.xlsx")[, c(1,3,9,13)]
label$Cross <- ifelse(label$Deoxynivalenol > 1000 & label$`Total DON` < 1250, "Cross-Negative",
                ifelse(label$Deoxynivalenol < 1000 & label$`Total DON` > 1250, "Cross-Positive", "None"))
# remove the none data
label <- label[label$Cross != "None", ]

# set as factor
label[,c(1, 2, 5)] <- lapply(label[, c(1, 2, 5)], as.factor)
str(label)

#melt the data for plotting
library(reshape2)
label_melt <- melt(label, id.vars = c("Sample_ID", "Cross"), measure.vars = c("Deoxynivalenol", "Total DON"), variable.name = "Toxin", value.name = "Concentration")

library(ggplot2)
library(ggpubr)

cross_label_plot <- ggplot(label_melt, aes(x = Sample_ID, y = Concentration, color = Cross, shape = Toxin)) +
                    # 1. Draw the 50% error bars first (so they sit cleanly behind the points)
                    geom_errorbar(
                        aes(ymin = Concentration * 0.5, ymax = Concentration * 1.5),
                        width = 0.3,                            
                        linewidth = 0.4,
                        position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)  
                    ) +
                    
                    # 2. Draw the actual measurement as a large, bold point
                    geom_point(
                        position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), 
                        size = 4, 
                        alpha = 0.9
                    ) +
                    
                    # 3. Add the regulatory thresholds
                    geom_hline(yintercept = 1000, linetype = "dashed", color = "#c0392b", linewidth = 0.8) +
                    geom_hline(yintercept = 1250, linetype = "dashed", color = "#2980b9", linewidth = 0.8) +
                    
                    # 4. Apply ggpubr's pristine academic theme
                    theme_pubr(base_size = 14) +
                    
                    # 5. Clean labeling
                    labs(
                        title = "Cross-label between Deoxynivalenol and Total DON",
                        x = "Sample ID",
                        y = "Concentration (ppb)",
                        color = NULL,
                        shape = NULL
                    ) +
                    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(300, 2300), breaks = seq(0, 2500, 500)) +
                    # 6. Formatting tweaks for readability
                    theme(
                        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
                        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
                        legend.position = "top"
                    )
ggsave("./figures/PLS_DA/cross_label_plot.svg", plot = cross_label_plot, width = 12, height = 6, units = "in", dpi =600)                    
```
## Comparison with mixed dataset model

```{r}
#import the mixed dataset model results
mixed_data <- list(
    "binary_1000" = read.csv("results/mixed_all/2_plsda_results.csv"),
    "binary_1250" = read.csv("results/mixed_all/2_plsda_results_1250.csv"),
    "weighted_1000" = read.csv("results/mixed_all/mix_weighted_triangle_plsda_result_1000.csv"),
    "weighted_1250" = read.csv("results/mixed_all/mix_weighted_triangle_plsda_results_1250.csv")
)
# remove all column except 1 - 5 and 16
mixed_data <- lapply(mixed_data, function(df) df[, c(1:5, 16)])

# remove Total_DON data on 1000 dataframes and DON data on 1250 dataframes
mixed_data$binary_1000 <- mixed_data$binary_1000[mixed_data$binary_1000$Target_toxin != "Total_DON", ]
mixed_data$weighted_1000 <- mixed_data$weighted_1000[mixed_data$weighted_1000$Target_toxin != "Total_DON", ]

# add details about the sample_weight
mixed_data$binary_1000$Sample_weight <- "None"
mixed_data$binary_1250$Sample_weight <- "None"
mixed_data$weighted_1000$Sample_weight <- "Weighted"
mixed_data$weighted_1250$Sample_weight <- "Weighted"

# combine all dataframes into one
combined_data_mix <- do.call(rbind, mixed_data)

#remove the second derivative data
combined_data_mix <- combined_data_mix[combined_data_mix$Preprocessing != "2nd_Der", ]
combined_data_mix$algorithm <- "Mixed"
combined_data_mix$MCC_z <- atanh(combined_data_mix$MCC)

combined_data_hierarchical <- combined_data
combined_data_hierarchical$algorithm <- "Hierarchical"
# combine the two datasets
combined_data_all <- rbind(combined_data_mix, combined_data_hierarchical)
combined_data_all[c(1:5, 7:8)] <- lapply(combined_data_all[c(1:5, 7:8)], as.factor)

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
# Fit the linear mixed-effects model
model3 <- lmer(MCC_z ~ (Sample_source + Target_toxin + Preprocessing + Variable_Selection + algorithm + Sample_weight)^3 + (1|Split), data = combined_data_all)
anova(model3)

```
